Aisha (eng-infra): quick RFC follow-up — thinking about decoupling the rate-limiter token-bucket from SLO enforcement. want to discuss interface boundaries and long-term refactor. who has bandwidth?
Ben (eng-platform): +1. curious what you mean by decouple — is this about making admission layer simpler and pushing SLO checks to policy?
Aisha (eng-infra): exactly. current monolith limiter does both accounting (tokens) and SLO decisions (reject/soft-shed). it's hard to test and swap algorithms. idea: split into a thin token service + an SLO policy engine that subscribes to telemetry.
Carlos (eng-runtime): sounds good. runtime cares about per-model latency budgets. how would we surface model-level SLOs to policy engine? via tag on the request?
Aisha (eng-infra): yes, attach metadata (model:id, tier, route). policy engine evaluates and returns an action: allow / queue / degrade / fallback. token service only answers availability queries.
Diane (eng-sre): > tradeoff: what about correctness during network partitions? if token service is down, we need safe fallback. current single component fails closed.
Aisha (eng-infra): proposal: conservative default is fail-open to preserve critical customers but emit high-severity alert + automatic traffic shaping to dedicated pools. also we can run local short-lived caches to avoid 100% dependency.
Ben (eng-platform): what about implementation surface? would this be gRPC API between runtime and policy? or REST?
Carlos (eng-runtime): prefer gRPC with bidi streaming for updates (policy signals, revised budgets). streaming lets runtime adapt without per-request roundtrip.
Aisha (eng-infra): agree. sketch of APIs: 
```
service TokenService {
  rpc CheckToken(CheckRequest) returns (CheckResponse); // fast path, allowed/denied + tokens_left
}
service PolicyEngine {
  rpc Eval(EvalRequest) returns (EvalResponse); // heavier: may consult historical telemetry
  rpc StreamSignals(stream Signal) returns (stream SignalAck);
}
```
Ben (eng-platform): nice. separate services means we can experiment with ML-based abuse detectors in the policy engine without touching token path.
Diane (eng-sre): ops question: metrics and SLOs for new components. token QPS needs tight P90 latency SLO. policy can be softer but needs correctness guarantees (no silent drops).
Aisha (eng-infra): plan: token service SLO 10ms p90, 50ms p99. policy engine p50 ~30ms, p95 ~200ms. runtime will have local hedging window: if policy timeout, fall back to token answer only.
Carlos (eng-runtime): hedging window sounds good. what about atomicity across multiple resources (tokens + KV cache + model capacity)? we sometimes need composite decision.
Aisha (eng-infra): composite decisions handled by policy engine; it can query multiple subsystems or read pre-joined telemetry. token service stays dumb.
Ben (eng-platform): migration path? we have 3 clusters using current limiter code. suggest adapter layer: keep old API but route to new services behind a feature flag.
Aisha (eng-infra): exactly — 4-step plan: 1) implement token svc + lightweight adapter, 2) add policy engine with default simple rules, 3) enable streaming signals, 4) roll out rule-driven AB tests and ML detectors.
Diane (eng-sre): rollback story? feature flag per-cluster, per-tenant. also autocircuit breaker if error rates spike.
Carlos (eng-runtime): one more: data retention & privacy for policy engine telemetry. some customers require short retention or on-prem policy instances.
Aisha (eng-infra): noted. policy engine must support per-tenant retention config and run in private deployments. also provide an opt-out for ML telemetry.
Ben (eng-platform): can we get a small prototype by end of sprint? I can help with adapter and integration tests.
Aisha (eng-infra): would love that. @planner-bot can you add RFC follow-up ticket and schedule a 30m sync?
planner-bot: created ticket INFRA-8321 and scheduled meeting 2026-04-14 10:00 UTC. :calendar:
Diane (eng-sre): +1 for meeting. I'll bring runbook changes and SLO error budgets.
Carlos (eng-runtime): I'll draft the runtime hedging patch and a test plan for composite decisions.
Aisha (eng-infra): thanks all — added the prototype tasks to INFRA-8321. will share initial API proto in the thread tomorrow.
Ben (eng-platform): thanks! :thumbsup:
